stem: An infant has a rounded area of consolidation on chest X-ray; why can pneumonia appear round in infants?

options.text: AP projection magnifies the opacity into a rounded shape
Pleural fluid traps the consolidation into a sphere
Collateral channels between alveoli are not well developed, so the pneumonia does not spread as readily
The thymus compresses the lung into a rounded shape
Collapse in children always forms a round lesion

explanation: Round pneumonia is due to underdeveloped collateral channels between alveoli, which limits spread of the infection and produces a rounded airspace consolidation in infants.
rationale: Round pneumonia is a rounded airspace consolidation in infants because collateral ventilation is not yet well developed.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because AP projection changes apparent size and shape on the image, but it does not cause round pneumonia.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because pleural fluid produces pleural effusion, not a rounded parenchymal consolidation.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because underdeveloped collateral channels limit interalveolar spread, so pneumonia can remain localised and appear round.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the thymus may alter mediastinal contour, but it does not explain round pneumonia.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because collapse does not always form a round lesion; round pneumonia is a distinct radiological pattern.
